problem.statement: Load an ESM-only npm package (e.g., chalk 5, node-fetch 3) from CommonJS code with require().

approach.summary: require("chalk") after upgrading to a major version that ships as pure ESM.

failure.point: Packages declaring "type": "module" without a CJS export cannot be require()d on Node < 22.12/20.17-era interop; the call throws ERR_REQUIRE_ESM.
failure.evidence: Node.js documentation of ERR_REQUIRE_ESM and the affected packages' own migration notes; workarounds are dynamic import(), staying on the last CJS major, or new-enough Node with require(esm) enabled.

environment.description: Node.js versions predating stable require(esm) support (roughly < 22.12 / < 23), CommonJS consumer.

transferability.notes: Recent Node versions can require() synchronous-graph ESM; check your runtime before treating this as a wall.
